summary: TechCrunch's The Station newsletter, hosted by Rebecca Bellan while Kirsten Korosec was at the Rebelle Rally, covers Tesla's weak Q3 earnings and Elon Musk's Cybertruck comments, the collapse of freight broker Convoy, and Rivian's first all-electric win at the Rebelle Rally. It also rounds up micromobility news, funding deals, and items on autonomous vehicles, EVs and charging, eVTOL, and people moves.
one_line: The Station newsletter covering Tesla's Q3 margin drop and Cybertruck remarks, Convoy's shutdown, Rivian's Rebelle Rally win, plus transportation deals and news.
key_facts: Tesla reported a Q3 gross margin of 17.9%, down from 25.1% a year earlier and from 18.2% in Q2; profits fell 44% to $1.85 billion.
Tesla's solar deployments slipped 48% in Q3 year over year, while energy storage deployments spiked 90%.
Tesla plans initial Cybertruck deliveries at an event at Giga Texas on November 30; Elon Musk said it will take 18 months to become profitable and said "we dug our own grave with Cybertruck."
Musk said Giga Texas will produce about 250,000 Cybertrucks a year starting in 2025; he had originally said the Cybertruck would be on the market by 2021.
Rebelle Rally 2023 is a 2,120-kilometer off-road navigation competition in its eighth year with 65 all-women teams, where GPS and electronic devices are prohibited.
A Rivian R1T team, driver Lillian Macaruso and navigator Alexandra Anderson (both Rivian employees), won the 4×4 class, the first time an all-electric vehicle topped the podium.
Convoy, a Seattle-based digital freight broker, shut down citing a "massive freight recession" about 18 months after raising $260 million at a $3.8 billion valuation.
Convoy CEO Dan Lewis said he found fewer than 30 startups going after trucking despite billions of dollars flowing into it each year.

Hayden AI raised a $53 million Series B led by the Drawdown Fund; Nirvana Insurance raised a $57 million Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners at a valuation above $350 million; Transfix raised a $40 million Series F.
Wallbox acquired the operations and assets of ABL for €15 million, aiming to deploy more than 1 million chargers globally.
Volta Trucks filed for bankruptcy proceedings in Sweden after the August bankruptcy of supplier Proterra and battery supplier uncertainty.

Cruise, General Motors and Honda will launch a robotaxi service with Origin vehicles in Tokyo in 2026, while NHTSA opened an investigation into Cruise's AV system after pedestrian incidents in San Francisco.
BMW Group and Toyota are adopting the NACS charging standard; BMW drivers gain Supercharger access in early 2025 and Toyota will build NACS-port vehicles from 2025.
Lucid delivered 1,457 Air sedans in Q3, missing Wall Street estimates by about 500 vehicles.
Flexport is laying off 20% of workers, about 600 people.
